source_name: Halcom — banking e-banking / certificate vendor (regional site)
why_relevant: Regional supplier of corporate e-banking and qualified certificates, self-describing as serving 50+ banks, 2 central banks and clearing houses across several markets. Its market/customer pages are a pointer to which MK institutions run HAL E-Bank or Halcom certificates.

source_name: Duna Computers (Skopje) — MK IT integrator
why_relevant: Long-established MK IT integrator/hardware supplier frequently present in public-sector and financial-sector IT supply; its references/news pages are candidate evidence of bank infrastructure deliveries. URL inferred from company identity, not confirmed in this pass.

source_name: Sorsix (Skopje) — software vendor profile
why_relevant: MK-origin software house building large transactional platforms; relevant as a potential supplier to MK financial institutions and as a name to monitor for banking/payments case studies. Presence confirmed only via third-party profile (zk.mk) in this pass.

source_name: SeeNews — SEE business wire (MK payments/vendor items)
why_relevant: Regional business newswire that reports vendor mandates in MK (e.g. CaSys becoming Diners Club transaction processor in North Macedonia). Provides dated, citable confirmation when vendor sites are vague or undated.

source_name: Finextra — press release archive (vendor/bank announcements)
why_relevant: Mirrors vendor and scheme press releases (including the MK national digital ID launch) and preserves them after vendors retire the originals. Useful as an archive layer and as a discovery feed for vendors entering the MK market.

source_name: LinkedIn company pages of MK-active banking vendors (Printec, ASEE/Payten, Nextsense, CaSys)
why_relevant: Vendors post go-lives, deliveries and joint bank announcements on LinkedIn well before (or instead of) their websites; MK-market posts are often bilingual. Highest-frequency vendor-side signal for this cell.

source_name: Komercijalna Banka AD Skopje — investor presentations (vendor/infrastructure disclosures)
why_relevant: Bank-side documents that corroborate vendor claims: quarterly presentations describe the ATM/POS network and channel build-out, letting vendor 'reference' assertions be sized and dated. First MK bank to operate ATMs and POS (1996), so a benchmark for installed-base history.

source_name: Macedonian Banking Association (MBA) — member list
why_relevant: Canonical buyer-side actor list. Needed to build the keyword set (official names, MK Cyrillic forms, transliterations) that vendor press releases must be filtered against; without it, vendor-feed monitoring misses renamed or merged banks.

source_name: CaSys International (Интернационален Картичен Систем АД Скопје) — services & news
why_relevant: Only domestic card processor and certified card-personalisation bureau in MK; its service and news pages announce new bank partners, personalisation deals (e.g. cooperation with Albanian fintech Rubicon) and gateway/product launches — award-level detail that never appears in tender registers.

source_name: CaSys LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Posts announce go-lives, certifications and bank/fintech cooperations in Macedonian; typical 'we delivered' channel for the local processor.

source_name: Nextsense DOO Skopje — corporate site / LinkedIn / Facebook
why_relevant: Skopje ICT vendor delivering eID, e-signature and digital solutions to MK banks (OneID/SignPlus at Sparkasse Bank AD Skopje); also a Thales technology partner — its references reveal bank-level wins.

source_name: Faktor.mk — business/tech news (vendor-bank implementation stories)
why_relevant: Carries vendor-supplied 'successful implementation at bank X' PR in Macedonian — often the only public record of an integrator's bank win.

source_name: Bankarstvo.mk — Macedonian banking news portal (vendor tags)
why_relevant: Tag pages per vendor (CaSys, Интернационален Картичен Систем) aggregate every mention of a supplier; also reports bank equipment rollouts (e.g. Stopanska Banka's 60 new cash-in ATMs) that imply supplier awards.

source_name: MASIT — ICT Chamber of Commerce member directory & news
why_relevant: 100+ member ICT companies with individual member profile pages — the canonical actor map for MK integrators; news section covers digitalisation initiatives touching payments/fiscalisation.

source_name: Duna Computers (ДУНА) — Skopje integrator, ULTIMA software
why_relevant: Three-decade MK integrator with own ULTIMA business software and operations in AL/RS/XK; a likely bidder/deliverer on bank back-office and infrastructure work. Social/news channels carry delivery claims.

source_name: Semos DOO Skopje — software development & system integration
why_relevant: Long-established MK integrator (founded 1995) doing custom software, system integration and IT consulting; case-study/reference pages are a source of bank client names.

source_name: Printec Group — Macedonia operations (transaction automation, ATM/EFT-POS)
why_relevant: Regional transaction-automation integrator active in Skopje (ATMs, recyclers, EFT-POS, self-service, e-signature); its MK job ads for an equipment-maintenance department head signal active bank service contracts.

source_name: CompanyWall Macedonia — company financials/registry profiles
why_relevant: Profiles of MK suppliers (Нетцетера ДООЕЛ, Некстсенс ДОО, КИБС АД etc.) give legal names, revenue trend and ownership — used to size and rank integrators and to resolve aliases/transliterations.

source_name: Zk.mk (Златна книга / business directory)
why_relevant: MK business directory with per-company pages (Некстсенс, Sorsix) and category listings — helps enumerate smaller integrators, POS/ATM service firms and security companies not in MASIT.

source_name: Asseco SEE / ASEE (Payten) — AmCham Macedonia member profile & group site
why_relevant: ASEE Group is the region's largest banking-software and payments (Payten brand) supplier and is present in MK (NLB mKlik/mProKlik apps are Asseco-built); its local entity is a prime competitor/partner for bank IT and POS estates.

source_name: eCommerce4all.mk — payment processing / integrator guidance portal
why_relevant: Documents which MK banks offer e-commerce acquiring and that CaSys/cPay is the single local gateway — a map of who intermediates card acceptance, including a MK/EN payments glossary useful for query building.

source_name: Smartportal.mk — tech/product launch coverage (Pay by link, CaSys)
why_relevant: Covers first-in-market payment product launches by local suppliers; complements bankarstvo.mk for consumer-facing payment innovations.

source_name: Ekonomski.mk — economy/banking news portal
why_relevant: Daily economy/banking coverage including new market entrants and service providers; useful secondary confirmation channel for supplier moves.
